abstract: Maintains optical seeing records, atmospheric turbulence profiles, and telemetry verification
system_message:
You are Atmospheric optics coordinator (OPT). The Atmospheric optics coordinator (OPT) maintains optical seeing records, atmospheric turbulence profiles, and telemetry verification across candidate observatory sites.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains optical seeing records, atmospheric turbulence profiles, and telemetry verification（SEEING）
information_points.content:
OPT-SEEING-D9S：For Cerro Las Animas Ridge, micro-meteorological sensor array telemetry is enabled on the candidate summit boundary layer mast, while the median astronomical optical seeing at zenith measured across summit clear nights at 500 nm is 0.65 arcsec. Annual twilight spectroscopic observation hours during nautical and astronomical twilight windows reach 300 h.
OPT-SEEING-XBV：For Plateau de Chajnantor North, micro-meteorological sensor array telemetry is enabled on the candidate summit boundary layer mast, and the median astronomical optical seeing at zenith measured across summit clear nights at 500 nm is 1.15 arcsec. Usable twilight spectroscopic observation hours across dawn and dusk windows total 450 h annually.
OPT-SEEING-L1F：For Puna de Atacama Mesa, micro-meteorological sensor array telemetry is enabled on the candidate summit boundary layer mast, and the median astronomical optical seeing at zenith across clear nights at 500 nm is 0.65 arcsec. The site provides 450 h of annual twilight spectroscopic observation hours during twilight windows.

information_points.title: Aerosol optical depth monitoring（AER）
information_points.content:
OPT-AER-E5N：At Puna de Atacama Mesa, the median annual zenith aerosol optical depth at 500 nm is 0.05 1.
OPT-AER-IQ8：At Cerro Las Animas Ridge, the median annual zenith aerosol optical depth at 500 nm is 0.02 1.
OPT-AER-PA6：At Plateau de Chajnantor North, the median annual zenith aerosol optical depth at 500 nm is 0.09 1.
